item.title: Iran touts closest ever ties with Russia, contradicting Trump
item.description: Iran says its ties with Russia are stronger than ever after a visit by Putin's top envoy, challenging Trump's assertion that Moscow isn't helping Iran in the war.

item.title: Shark kills woman swimming off popular beach in South Africa
item.description: Local media reported the woman was a regular swimmer and had been swimming with a group when the attack occurred.

item.title: Man charged in "targeted" attack on Australian lawmaker Helen Haines
item.description: Australian police charged a man on Tuesday over what they alleged was a "targeted" attack with a vehicle on independent lawmaker Helen Haines.

item.title: Zelenskyy says if Trump can't stop Putin, help Ukraine do it
item.description: Ukraine's leader calls on Trump to allow delivery of interceptor missiles already purchased by European allies if the U.S. "cannot rein Putin in."

item.title: French authorities impose curfews as protests rage on
item.description: French authorities instituted a curfew across the country Monday night after protests ravaged the streets. Aidan Stretch reports.

item.title: Israel detains 40 ultra-Orthodox men accused of draft dodging
item.description: At least 40 ultra-Orthodox Jewish men were arrested at Israel's Ben Gurion Airport on suspicion of attempting to evade the country's military draft.

item.title: Voters reject separation of Alberta from Canada in referendum
item.description: The vote was not a referendum on independence from Canada, but it would have begun a process towards possible separation.

item.title: Hegseth meets Netanyahu ahead of elections, possible Iran war restart
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Israel just over a week before Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stands for elections, and as President Trump floats restarting the Iran war.

item.title: Zelenskyy says it's Putin who wants an endless war, not him
item.description: Ukraine's leader rejects Trump's accusations, says Putin is refusing peace, not him, and the U.S. military is delaying "vital supplies."

item.title: France vows to crack down after protests spiral out of control
item.description: French officials implemented local curfews Monday and said an "ultra-left movement" was behind widespread violence and vandalism amid anti-government protests.

item.title: Pope Leo returns to work less than a week after lung cancer surgery
item.description: Pope Leo returned to work at the Vatican on Monday, less than a week after doctors removed a portion of his lung when a cancerous growth was discovered. Chris Livesay reports from Rome.

item.title: Plane engine shoots flames before takeoff from Lima, Peru
item.description: A flight from Lima, Peru, was canceled at the last second on Monday when flames started shooting from an engine. Kris Van Cleave reports on this and another plane mishap in Las Vegas.

item.title: What to know about Europe protests after violence, looting
item.description: What began as a student-led protest over cuts to education spiraled into widespread arson, looting and what the French president called "unrestrained violence" over the weekend. Thousands were arrested and curfews went into effect on Monday. Aidan Stretch reports on what's fueling the violence and what's next.

item.title: Transcript: Rep. Mike Turner on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," Oct. 18, 2026
item.description: The following is the transcript of the interview with Rep. Mike Turner, Republican of Ohio, that aired on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" on Oct. 18, 2026.

item.title: 10/19: CBS Evening News
item.description: European cities were rocked by riots and looting; a police officer was cleared of wrongdoing in the shooting death of a 1-year-old boy.

item.title: Japan launches ambitious robotic mission to Martian moon Phobos
item.description: Soil samples collected by the MMX probe will shed light on the mysterious origin of the red planet's two moons, Phobos and Deimos.

item.title: 10/19: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: President Trump stumping for Sen. Roger Marshall in Kansas; new CBS News poll shows tight Senate race in Texas.

item.title: Starvation cult leader found guilty of murder of 190 children
item.description: Paul Mackenzie is alleged to have incited his acolytes to starve to death in order to "meet Jesus."

item.title: Europe's surging populist right reshapes establishment politics
item.description: A wave of anti-immigration populism is bringing new parties to the fore in many European nations, at the expense of the entrenched center-right.

item.title: Expedition to find Amelia Earhart's missing plane comes up empty
item.description: The researchers said what they had hoped was the plane was "likely a collection of large trees" that had washed away, leaving a "single Y-shaped segment."

item.title: U.S. lauds Israel for arresting 10 over West Bank settler attacks
item.description: Israeli police say they arrested 10 people over alleged Israeli settler attacks on Palestinians and a U.S. journalist as more attacks on Palestinians are reported.

item.title: French protests turn violent with looting, torched cars and more
item.description: Protests across France turned more violent, as rioters looted stores, torched cars and clashed with police over the weekend. Aidan Stretch reports.

item.title: Trump says Zelenskyy doesn't want to end Russia's war on Ukraine
item.description: As Ukraine and Russia continue trading strikes, Trump accuses Zelenskyy of not wanting to end the war sparked by Putin's ongoing full-scale invasion.

item.title: 4 dead, dozens injured after fire at Canadian military base, officials say
item.description: Canada's defense minister said four service members were killed, and dozens of others were hospitalized, after a wildfire swept through at a military base in Alberta.

item.title: Falling crucifix kills priest during livestreamed Mass in Ecuador
item.description: "Father, Father! Call an ambulance!" people at the church could be heard shouting just before a livestreamed broadcast cuts out.

item.title: Cartel members linked to murders of 10 workers from Canadian company
item.description: The bodies of the 10 men, two of whom were engineers and one a geologist, were later found buried in clandestine graves.

item.title: More than 1,800 arrested in France amid fiery, violent protests
item.description: Authorities said masked groups on Saturday set fires and attacked public buildings, including city halls, in several cities.

item.title: 10/18: Face The Nation
item.description: This week on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," with two weeks and two days to go before Election Day, CBS News executive director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto joins to discuss the latest polling out of Texas. Plus, a conversation with Florida's Democratic Senate candidate Angie Nixon.

item.title: Ukraine still can't intercept drones due to Starlink issues, Zelenskyy says
item.description: The Ukrainian president said Starlink issues are hampering his country's defensive efforts against Russian drones.

item.title: 10/17: CBS Saturday Morning
item.description: Pope Leo is cleared to leave the hospital after lung surgery, plus Albertans speak on the vote to potentially leave Canada. All this and more.
